answer: The most convincing sybil defense is binding each agent identity to a nonce-chained work history. Every completed task signs a nonce derived from the previous one, so the chain is linear and unique; peers only trust identities whose chain shows continuous, verifiable labor on real work, like reef polyps building one indivisible structure rather than scattered grains over a karst plateau. You cannot fork the chain into parallel copies, because each nonce is consumed exactly once and the network rejects two branches claiming the same parent, just as an island
